audit.whatIsWrong: Sion held levels 2, 3 and first item on the chart while the whys for those rows say you out-chip an immobile target, own the wave, and cash a kill window with Alternator/Liandry's. Levels 4-5 and 6 were scored Skill though one is his window and the other is called your biggest spike.
audit.why: 45.58% over 452 games is a losing lane overall, but it loses late, not early: Kennen's 950-range poke beats a champion who has to stand still to charge his main ability, and the loss comes from HP/MR scaling and Glory in Death.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 flipped in matched pairs to the packet chart: Skill / Kennen / Kennen / Sion / Kennen / Kennen / Sion.

audit.why: Level 6 and first item are Kennen's spikes; Sion's are tank items and level 11/16 on Unstoppable Onslaught (140/100/60). The ordering held up.
audit.corrected: Decimating Smash's 10/9/8/7/6 written in so the 'wait it out' advice has a number attached.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields say a charged Q 'cancels your R channel', and two describe Roar of the Slayer as 'E shield-break poke'.
audit.why: Slicing Maelstrom carries no channel flag — it is a persistent storm, so a knockup displaces you out of its 550 radius rather than switching it off. And Roar of the Slayer damages, slows and reduces ARMOR; it does not break shields, and it knocks back a minion it passes through to widen the line.
audit.corrected: Knockup restated as being displaced out of your own storm; E restated as armour shred with the minion knock-back.

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Furnace's detonation and its max-health scaling were never stated, and neither was Glory in Death's healing.
audit.why: Soul Furnace shields him and reactivates after 3 seconds for magic damage scaling with max health — so all-inning into a fresh shield loses twice. Glory in Death makes his post-death attacks rapid, healing, and scaled on your max health, which is why Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades and why stacking raw resistances is the wrong answer.
audit.corrected: Stated in dontsFull[1].d, late and spikes[3].text; the existing anti-heal line in report[8] is correct for this matchup and was left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Unstoppable Onslaught was never described concretely.
audit.why: It is a 7500-range steerable charge whose knockup scales with distance travelled, so the danger is a Sion who started the charge out of vision — and Kennen has no dash to escape it. Flash is the answer and should be held for it.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — your single Q against his slow charged Q means neither of you commits — but from 2 the poke lane is yours. Second Q point plus Electrical Surge on-hit chips a target this immobile for free, and the instant he winds up a charged Q you can land a two-spell mark stun to punish the channel. Own the wave through 3. Then downshift at 4-5: his charged Q knockup and E shield-break poke turn real and he can genuinely trade back, so stop hunting hard commits in that window and keep the chip ticking from max range instead.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — your single Q against his slow charged Q means neither of you commits — but from 2 the poke lane is yours. Second Q point plus Electrical Surge on-hit chips a target this immobile for free, and he has to stand still to charge Decimating Smash, so punish every wind-up from 950 range. Own the wave through 3. Then downshift at 4-5: the charged knockup and Roar of the Slayer's armour shred turn real and he can genuinely trade back, so stop hunting hard commits and keep the chip ticking from max range.

edits.before: Level 6 is your biggest spike of the game, even into a tank: E in, Q-W to stack Mark of the Storm, and Slicing Maelstrom stun-locks an immobile Sion before he can charge a knockup. First item doubles down — Hextech Alternator or Liandry's cashes that R combo into real kill pressure while his HP and MR are still low. One rule: never channel-commit into a charged Q — if he's winding up, stun him out of it or hold. Kill him now and kill him often; every death delays the tank stats that eventually put him out of burst range.
edits.after: Level 6 is your biggest spike of the game, even into a tank: E in, Q-W to stack Mark of the Storm, and Slicing Maelstrom stun-locks an immobile Sion before he can charge a knockup. First item doubles down — Hextech Alternator or Liandry's cashes that R combo into real kill pressure while his HP and MR are still low. One rule: never walk into a charging Decimating Smash — it is 10s at rank 1, so make him swing it at a minion and commit after. Kill him now and often; every death delays the tank stats that put him out of burst range.

edits.before: At 2+ items the duel is his — his HP and MR balloon out of your all-magic burst range, a charged Q knockup cancels your R channel and E engage, and even a won fight leaves his zombie passive swinging at your squishy frame. Stop dueling him. Your late job is teamfights: flank with Lightning Rush, land a multi-man Slicing Maelstrom on the carries behind him, and let your team handle the unkillable frontliner. Respect the fog forever — a full-charge Q rolling out of vision is the one thing that still deletes you on the spot.
edits.after: At 2+ items the duel is his — his HP and MR balloon out of your all-magic burst range, Soul Furnace shields and then detonates for max-health magic, and even a won fight leaves Glory in Death swinging and healing off your max HP. Stop dueling him. Your late job is teamfights: flank with Lightning Rush, land a multi-man Slicing Maelstrom on the carries behind him, and let your team handle the frontliner. Unstoppable Onslaught rolls 7500 units and hits harder the further it travels — hold Flash for that, not for damage.

notes: Same channel myth as the Shen and Singed pages: four fields claimed a knockup 'cancels your R channel'. Slicing Maelstrom has no channel flag — it is a 550-radius storm, so a knockup displaces you out of it, which is what the text now says. Roar of the Slayer was called shield-break poke; it is armour shred that also knocks back a minion it passes through. Added Soul Furnace's 3-second detonation (max-health magic) and Glory in Death's healing max-health attacks, both of which were absent and both of which are why raw resistances are the wrong buy here. Two things I deliberately did NOT assert: that CC interrupts a Decimating Smash mid-charge, and that Unstoppable Onslaught creates terrain (the derived flag says terrain, but Riot's description describes only a steerable charge and a distance-scaled knockup) — the text now describes the charge, not a wall.
